findings.title: requireNonNull check is on grantType, not rawTokenId
findings.body: The fourth null-check is `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`. The argument is `grantType` (copied from the previous line) and the message wrongly refers to `rawTokenId`. The intended line is `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`. As written, a null `rawTokenId` passes silently, which later causes a "null:<uuid>" string in `encodeTokenId` or an NPE for consumers of `getRawTokenId()`.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has wrong substring indices and inverted condition
findings.body:
The new `isAccessTokenId` matcher does `items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut) return false;`. There are two independent bugs here:

1. The prefix is 6 chars `ST TT GG` where the grant shortcut is at indices 4..5 (0-based), so it should be `substring(4, 6)`. With the current indices the value extracted is "ta" for any well-formed token id, so it never equals any real grant shortcut (`ac`, `rt`, `dg`, `ci`, ...).
2. The condition is inverted: when the substring DOES match the expected shortcut the matcher returns `false` (fail), when it does NOT match it falls through to the UUID check and returns `true` (pass).

Net effect: the matcher enforces only the UUID format and never actually checks the encoded grant shortcut, so `expectCodeToToken`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, and `expectAuthReqIdToToken` will continue to pass even if the token ID has the wrong (or no) grant shortcut. The correct body is approximately `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false; return isUUID().matches(items[1]);`.

findings.title: Javadoc says "3-letters shortcut" but all implementations are 2-letter
findings.body: The Javadoc on `getShortcut()` says "usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants" but every factory added in this PR (`ac`, `cc`, `ro`, `rt`, `dg`, `ci`, `te`, `pc`, `pg`, plus `na` for unknown) and the `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` itself rely on a 2-character fixed width (the tokenizer even asserts `encodedContext.length() != 6`). The doc string should be corrected to "2-letters" (or simply "short") so future implementers do not accidentally introduce 3-character shortcuts that will silently fail to decode.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType catches RuntimeException too broadly
findings.body: `testIncorrectGrantType` does `catch (RuntimeException iae) { /* ignored */ }`. `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId` is documented to throw `IllegalArgumentException` for an unknown grant shortcut, but the test will also treat unrelated runtime errors (NPE, IllegalStateException, etc.) as "expected". The assertion should catch `IllegalArgumentException` (or `assertThrows(IllegalArgumentException.class, () -> ...)`) and the wrong-shape test data (`ofrtac:5678`) should be revisited in light of the substring bug in `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId`.
